validated_results.title: Both serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and calcium levels may increase the risk of incident prostate cancer in Caribbean men of African ancestry.
validated_results.reason: This case-control study evaluated the association between serum calcium concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk in Jamaican men.

extraction.population: Men 40-80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer and controls

sample_size.excerpt: Nine hundred and seventy-two men were interviewed and 243 men with newly diagnosed PCa and 275 controls were enrolled; negative biopsy men ( n = 187) and men who did not meet the inclusion criteria for controls ( n = 267) were excluded from analyses. In this report, we present information on calcium (224 cases; 248 controls) and 25(OH)D vitamin D (146 cases; 191 controls) for whom a sample of blood was available.
sample_size.location: Table 5; total_n derived from reported group counts 243 + 224 + 9 = 476

effect_size.excerpt: Multivariable-adjusted models showed a positive linear relationship between PCa and serum calcium (OR, 1.12; CI, 1.00–1.25 per 0.1 nmol/L). Serum 25(OH)D concentration also showed a positive association with PCa (OR, 1.23; CI, 1.01–1.49 per 10 ng/mL).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Serum calcium was positively correlated with PCa diagnosis (multivariable-adjusted: OR, 1.12; CI, 1.00–1.25 per 0.1 nmol/L).

design.excerpt: We examined these relationships in a case–control study of men 40–80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed PCa in Jamaica

timing.excerpt: We examined these relationships in a case–control study of men 40–80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed PCa in Jamaica

continent.excerpt: PCa in Jamaica, a tropical country
